clue.text: Puzzled when fellow sailor capsized and scarpered

indicators.note: a capsized boat is turned upside down, so the letters before it are turned round

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow
AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
to scarper is to run away; 'and' simply joins on

explanation.surface: Someone is bewildered when a shipmate overturned the boat and ran off.
explanation.walkthrough: The fellow and the sailor are capsized as one unit, not separately, before the running-away part is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To be baffled is to be confused and unable to understand, a direct synonym of puzzled.

clue.text: Dwarf who's up for a fight?

blocks.note: one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White, the shy one
read whimsically, the name splits as a word for a blow or brawl plus a suffix meaning 'full of', so someone full of fighting

explanation.surface: Which little fellow is spoiling for a scrap?
explanation.walkthrough: The shy dwarf's name, BASHFUL, is reread as BASH-FUL, full of bashes, the opposite of his timid nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Bashful is the name of the timid member of Disney's seven dwarfs in Snow White.

clue.text: Rove about in mink for warmth

indicators.note: moving about suggests the letters wander out of their order
in places the jumbled letters inside the other word

blocks.note: mink is a valuable fur
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wanders around wrapped in a mink coat to keep warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rove' looks like the main verb of the surface, but it is only letters to be jumbled and wrapped in the coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Fervour is intense passion or enthusiasm, the figurative warmth of strong feeling.

clue.text: Keeps dog from running off to fields over the hilltop

definitions.note: describes what the thing does rather than naming it; the answer is a noun

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter
in a down clue, over places one piece above the next

blocks.note: a lea is a meadow or field, a poetic word
the first letter of hill

explanation.surface: A dog is stopped from bolting off across the fields and over the brow of the hill.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a leash is what keeps a dog from running off.
explanation.definitionFit: A leash is the lead or strap attached to a dog's collar to restrain it.

clue.text: Helpful to have rebels' aid in revolution

indicators.note: something in revolution is being turned over and thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the two words supply the nine letters

explanation.surface: Insurgents in an uprising find outside help useful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' fits the rebels' story, but it is telling us to rearrange their letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something desirable is worth having or wanted, so it is advantageous to possess.

clue.text: Debs' semi-celebration at court is not done any more

indicators.note: semi means half, so only half of the neighbouring word is kept

blocks.note: taken as written; only its first half is used
a celebration is fun, a bit of merrymaking
CT is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: The debutantes' coming-out ball at the royal court has fallen out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Debs are debutantes, upper-class girls once presented at court. Half of DEBS gives DE, then FUN and CT.
explanation.definitionFit: Defunct means no longer existing or in use, so a defunct custom is no longer practised.

clue.text: Heard Donna Karan tops don't last

indicators.note: the tops of the words are their opening letters
what is heard is spoken, so the sound of the letters matters, not their spelling

blocks.note: the designer's initials, D and K, said as two letter names

explanation.surface: Designer fashion items, it's said, wear out quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Donna Karan is the New York designer behind the DKNY label; her initials spoken aloud make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that decay rot or fall apart over time, so they fail to endure.

clue.text: Sent on by car with journalist to cover fighting

indicators.note: to cover something is to wrap around it, so one piece goes outside the other

blocks.note: a Ford is a make of car
war is armed fighting
ED, editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A war correspondent is dispatched by car to report on the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' is only a link; the car brand wraps the fighting before the journalist is tacked on.
explanation.definitionFit: Mail that is forwarded is sent on from one address to a new one.

clue.text: Short book number five by Ms Fitzgerald

blocks.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
V is the Roman numeral for five
Ella Fitzgerald, the American jazz singer

explanation.surface: A slim volume, the fifth in a series, written by a woman named Fitzgerald.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a work of fiction longer than a short story but shorter than a novel.

clue.text: Credible chart about space

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: a table is a chart of figures
an en is a printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: A believable diagram concerning outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printing measure of space; TABLE goes around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenable theory can be held or defended, so it is believable and reasonable.

clue.text: Son quietly studies broadcasts

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to read a subject is to study it at university

explanation.surface: A boy reads silently while programmes go out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasts' is a verb here: sows or disseminates widely.
explanation.definitionFit: To spread news is to broadcast it, distributing it widely to many people.

clue.text: Trailer for vehicle (a light goods vehicle)

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
taken as written
a van carries light goods

explanation.surface: A towed unit for a vehicle, with a parenthetical note that the vehicle is a van.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a gloss on the first vehicle but supplies two more pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A caravan is a mobile home towed behind a car, a type of trailer in British usage.

clue.text: Reckless to hoodwink Nelson's mate

blocks.note: to hoodwink is to fool or trick
Captain Hardy, to whom the dying Nelson supposedly said 'Kiss me, Hardy'

explanation.surface: It is rash to try to deceive Admiral Nelson's right-hand man.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy was Nelson's flag captain at Trafalgar.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardy means rashly bold, taking needless risks without thought of the consequences.

clue.text: Improvise notices back to back, abridging the last

indicators.note: abridging shortens something, here the final one of the pair loses a letter
the second item is set back to front against the first

blocks.note: two kinds of notice: an advertisement, AD, and a poster, BILL

explanation.surface: Instructions to wing it with the posters, pasting them back to back and cutting the last one short.
explanation.walkthrough: The notices are AD and BILL; BILL is shortened to BIL and turned round to sit back to back with AD.
explanation.definitionFit: To ad-lib is to speak or perform without preparation, making it up on the spot.

clue.text: Insects come from this river in volcanic rock

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the answer, a noun

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: lava is molten rock from a volcano
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Bugs emerge from a stream running through a lava field.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature grub stage from which an adult insect develops.

clue.text: Lost for words at a stitch-up over lorry

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
in a down clue, over sets the first pieces above the last

blocks.note: 'at' links; the article is taken as written
to stitch is to sew
a lorry is the British word for a truck

explanation.surface: Someone is speechless after a fit-up involving a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: A stitch-up is British slang for a frame-up; here it splits into stitch plus up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone awestruck is so filled with wonder that they are rendered speechless.

clue.text: Could love in Shakespeare's play be trivial pursuit?

definitions.note: an example: Trivial Pursuit is a well-known one

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: Shakespeare is the Bard
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a game is play

explanation.surface: Could romance in a Shakespeare comedy be a frivolous pastime?
explanation.walkthrough: Lower-case 'trivial pursuit' hides the capitalised board game Trivial Pursuit, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trivial Pursuit is a famous quiz played on a board, so it is one instance of the category.

clue.text: Claim first son has trouble in store

indicators.note: trouble stirs things up, so the following letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: A is first, as in A1 or grade A
S is the abbreviation for son
the seven letters are taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An allegation that the eldest boy is heading for difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble in store' reads as a set phrase, but 'in store' is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An assertion is a confident statement of fact or belief, the same as a claim.

clue.text: Sample a smaller amount, when flavour's lacking

blocks.note: to sample food is to taste it
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Try only a little of the dish when it has no flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteless food is bland, having no flavour at all.

clue.text: No longer interested in plan for diet

indicators.note: to plan is to arrange, so the letters are laid out in a new order

blocks.note: the seven letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A dieter has lost enthusiasm for their eating regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plan for diet' reads as a meal plan; 'plan' is the signal and 'for diet' the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To be tired of something is to be bored with it and have lost enthusiasm.

clue.text: Coastal city's main support for bird

indicators.note: in a down clue, a support sits below what it holds up

blocks.note: a swan is a bird
the main is an old word for the open sea

explanation.surface: A seaside city relies on its ocean to keep a seabird afloat.
explanation.walkthrough: SEA supports SWAN by sitting beneath it. Swansea is a coastal city in south Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a port city on the south coast of Wales, so it is a city by the sea.

clue.text: Daughter best sort out what's owing

indicators.note: to sort out is to rearrange into a fresh order

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A daughter had better settle her outstanding bills.
explanation.definitionFit: Debts are sums of money that are owed to someone.

clue.text: Second-rate artist getting V&A event? Empty boasting!

blocks.note: B grade is second-rate
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
the initials taken as written
a do is a party or event

explanation.surface: A mediocre painter lands a show at the V&A and brags hollowly about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a showy display of boldness meant to impress, often hiding a lack of real courage.

clue.text: Looks at regulations first off for play equipment

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter is taken away

blocks.note: to look at something is to see it
laws are regulations

explanation.surface: An inspector checks the safety rules for playground apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: Seesaws are balanced planks children ride up and down in a playground.

clue.text: Criticise severely, when cutting corruption

indicators.note: cutting into something means going inside it

blocks.note: rot is decay or corruption
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone is lambasted for slicing into a corrupt scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When' looks like a link word but supplies the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast someone is informally to attack or mock them harshly.

clue.text: Ben running race in wild weather

indicators.note: running suggests letters in motion, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: Ben-Hur, the epic, so the name that follows Ben
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: A man called Ben runs a race in a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben-Hur, of the chariot race, completes Ben. 'In' looks like a link to the definition but is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hurricane is a violent tropical storm with very strong winds.

clue.text: Flier for leisure activity

blocks.note: first meaning: a small falcon
second meaning: a pastime pursued for pleasure

explanation.surface: A pilot who flies for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird meaning is less familiar: the hobby is a small swift falcon.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a species of falcon and an activity done regularly for pleasure.

clue.text: Scale for one finger

blocks.note: first meaning: a measure or indicator, as in a price scale
second meaning: the forefinger next to the thumb

explanation.surface: A musician practises a scale using a single finger.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a numerical indicator or measuring scale and also the pointing forefinger.

clue.text: Unsettle dicky birds round bath briefly

indicators.note: dicky means faulty or unsound, so the word next to it is put into disorder
briefly means cut short, so the final letter goes
round means surrounding, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written for rearranging
a tub is a bath

explanation.surface: Disturbing the ailing birds gathered around a birdbath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky birds' looks like the nursery phrase; dicky is British slang for unreliable or poorly.
explanation.definitionFit: To disturb is to upset or agitate someone, making them uneasy.

clue.text: Popular princess in a state

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
Diana, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: A much-loved princess is in an agitated condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' reads as 'upset'; the US state is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty United States, in the Midwest.

clue.text: Put trimmed joint in to cook without any frills

indicators.note: trimmed means a little is cut off the end
put in means placed inside

blocks.note: to fry is to cook
the ankle is a joint

explanation.surface: A recipe: place a cut-down joint of meat in to cook, keeping it plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' suggests meat, but it is the body joint at the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking frankly means speaking plainly and honestly, without embellishment.

clue.text: Deadly beast on island is captured by common sense

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor

blocks.note: an ox is a beast
I is the abbreviation for island
nous is practical intelligence

explanation.surface: A deadly animal on an island is caught by sensible people.
explanation.walkthrough: Nous is informal British for common sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Noxious means harmful or poisonous, potentially lethal.
